ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 concerning Combating Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing (as amended), Executive Regulations issued pursuant to Prime Ministerial Decree No. 2411 of 2002 (as further amended), read together with Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, Companies Law No. 159 of 1981, and the Central Bank of Egypt and Financial Regulatory Authority KYC regulations. No standalone public UBO register has yet been enacted; UBO identification is enforced through AML/CFT customer due diligence duties and GAFI investment file declarations.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: All UBOs, directors, and authorized signatories must be screened against the Egyptian Money Laundering and Terrorist Financing Combating Unit (EMLCU) consolidated sanctions and domestic terrorist list, the United Nations Security Council consolidated list, the US OFAC SDN list, and the European Union consolidated financial sanctions list. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any objective connection to a Politically Exposed Person, as required by Law No. 80 of 2002 and FATF standards. Screening evidence, transaction monitoring, and risk classification must be archived for AML audit purposes.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) E-Services Portal / Egyptian Commercial Registry System (https://www.eregistry.gafi.gov.eg; https://www.investinegypt.gov.eg)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The official company name must be in Arabic. A parallel transliterated version in Latin characters may be registered for international brand use, but the Arabic name remains authoritative for registry and judicial purposes. Any foreign-language name must be translated or transliterated into Arabic in the Memorandum of Association and Commercial Registry filings. Availability analysis is conducted using the Arabic orthography and phonetic equivalents to avoid deceptive similarity with existing registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the chosen name is rejected, the applicant may submit a written grievance via the GAFI e-services portal within 15 working days from the date of rejection, paying the EUR/EGP administrative fee equivalent of USD 25. GAFI's internal grievance committee must issue its decision within 10 working days. If the name is still refused, judicial review may be pursued before the Administrative Court of the Egyptian State Council within 60 days from notification of the final administrative decision. A single extension of the name reservation for an additional 30 days is possible upon written request and payment of the prescribed fee before the original reservation expires.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not recognized as a statutory head office for an Egyptian LLC; a physical registered office in Egypt evidenced by a lease or ownership agreement is mandatory. A professionally serviced or communal office may be accepted if a formal sublease agreement exists in the company's name, a dedicated workspace is identifiable, and an on-site administrative contact is available. Virtual-only addresses without a physical presence will be rejected by GAFI and the Commercial Registry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: A quantified risk of approximately 20% for an unannounced physical inspection during the first year of operation, mainly driven by VAT registration and e-commerce audit priorities. The likelihood declines to under 5% after the company has filed accurate tax returns and demonstrated commercial substance for at least one annual cycle.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 83 of 2022 on Companies (Qanoun Al-Sharikat), as amended, particularly Chapter 3 governing Limited Liability Companies (Articles 48-75), Articles 1-12 on incorporation, and the Executive Regulations issued thereunder; Law No. 34 of 1976 on the Commercial Register; and relevant provisions of Investment Law No. 72 of 2017, as amended, to the extent applicable.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Department, One-Stop Shop, including electronic filing via GAFI’s investor services portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Articles of Association / Contract of Incorporation in Arabic, submitted through GAFI’s electronic company registration platform, culminating in the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Qayd).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Law No. 83 of 2022 for LLCs; however, the share capital must be expressly stated in the Articles of Association and be sufficient to achieve the objects of the company. Monetary contributions must be deposited into a temporary blocked bank account at a licensed Egyptian bank prior to registration. The bank retains the funds until GAFI issues the Certificate of Incorporation, after which the capital is released to the company’s active bank account in the name of the LLC.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The incorporators subscribe to and take up the entire issued share capital, in the allocations stated in the share subscription schedule signed as part of the Articles of Association. (2) The registered office and principal place of business shall be located at [address], Egypt, within the jurisdiction of the Suez Canal Economic Zone. (3) The shareholders' general meeting hereby appoints the following officers: [Manager A] as Chief Executive Officer, [Manager B] as Finance Director, and [Manager C] as Compliance Manager, each with authority to open bank accounts, execute agreements, and complete all regulatory filings. (4) This resolution is effective immediately and shall remain binding until revoked or superseded.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: GAFI – Commercial Names Department / Investor Services Center (online portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log onto the GAFI electronic investment portal and submit three proposed company names in Arabic, together with the desired Latin transliteration if applicable, selecting the LLC suffix. Pay the name reservation fee and receive the digital name approval certificate, valid for 120 days.
required_dossiers: Executive summary of the business object (ISIC 4791 online retail)
Passport or national ID copies of all proposed shareholders
Power of attorney if a corporate shareholder or third-party service provider acts
Completed name application form on GAFI portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or conflicts with an existing mark, submit a written objection to GAFI with supporting search results and simultaneously resubmit alternative names.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Justice – Notary Public (or GAFI-integrated electronic notary for e-authentication)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Arabic Articles of Association containing company name, object, capital structure, registered office, board of managers, auditor, financial year, and dispute resolution. All incorporators or their attorneys-in-fact must sign before a Notary Public; notarization shall be affixed to the submitted copy.
required_dossiers: Name approval certificate
Draft Articles of Association in Arabic
Valid identification documents for shareholders and managers
Registered office lease contract or preliminary lease agreement
Written consent of managers to act as officers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary queries signatures or wording, execute a corrective notarial declaration or amend the Articles by notarial addendum.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening Temporary Bank Account and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Egyptian licensed bank selected by the shareholders (regulated by the Central Bank of Egypt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary company account for capital contributions at the chosen bank; each owner contributes their allocated portion. The bank will issue a certificate of capital deposit or blocked funds statement to be filed with GAFI. The funds shall remain blocked until the incorporation certificate is issued.
required_dossiers: Notarized preliminary Articles of Association
Tax ID or tax assessment for non-resident investors (where requested)
Name certificate and draft object
Passports or national IDs and anti-money laundering declaration forms
Bank's customer due-diligence forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: For bank refusal on documentary grounds, provide the bank with additional corporate documentation or obtain a GAFI directive/resolution letter instructing the bank to open the special account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: GAFI Incorporation Filing and Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the electronic dossier through the GAFI portal with notarized Articles, bank deposit certificate, name approval, and consent forms. GAFI reviewers examine legal compliance and issue the Certificate of Incorporation (Shahadat Al-Qayd) once satisfied, simultaneously registering the company in GAFI's companies ledger.
required_dossiers: Name approval certificate
Notarized Articles of Association
Bank capital deposit certificate
Consent of managers and auditor
Registered office lease contract
GAFI standard application forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, GAFI issues a deficiencies notice; applicants must cure the defect within 30 days via the portal, and any rejection can be challenged by written petition to GAFI's appeals unit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial Register Office attached to the Ministry of Supply and Internal Trade; Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) offices
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File with the Commercial Register to obtain the Commercial Registration Certificate; then register simultaneously with ETA for corporate income tax, payroll tax, VAT, and e-invoicing integration (Salamat). The tax registration must be completed within 30 days of the commercial registration.
required_dossiers: Certificate of Incorporation
Commercial registration application
Tax card forms (including ETA Form 1), company statute, and ID documents
Proof of registered office
Bank account details and expected activity declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of delay, submit an amended form through the ETA electronic filing system; if the Commercial Register stalls, obtain a certificate of acceptance and escalate to the head of the local registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating License and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Municipality (local administration) and Civil Defense Authority of the Ministry of Interior
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the commercial business license application ('Rekhsa Tashghil') to the district office covering the registered address, indicating online retail and warehouse activity for automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories. Obtain Civil Defense approval after inspection, pay municipal fees, and collect the operating license.
required_dossiers: Commercial Registration Certificate
Tax card / ETA registration receipt
Lease contract and address ownership documents
Civil Defense fire safety inspection report
Municipal license application form and fee receipts
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality objects, submit a technical rectification dossier, including corrected fire safety measures, and appeal to the governorate's licensing committee after receiving the rejection grounds.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Trade and Industry – Internal Trade Development Authority; District Municipality as the physical commercial-facility licensing authority
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Commercial Business Operation License (Rukhsat Tashghil Al-Manashaat)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Egyptian Environmental Affairs Agency (EEAA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – low-impact commercial/warehousing activity; full EIA Report not required. An automatic environmental registration/self-assessment is filed with EEAA, subject to waste-management compliance conditions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial process wastewater discharge or VOC emissions beyond domestic background thresholds. Must maintain segregated waste containers for spent automotive parts, including batteries, oils, filters, and packaging, and execute disposal contracts with licensed carriers in accordance with Law No. 202 of 2020 on Waste Management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety and Civil Defense Certificate issued after inspection of the office and warehouse, requiring fire extinguishers, alarm system, unobstructed exits, and compliance with load limits; structural load certificate issued by municipal engineers for stockroom shelving; and workplace clearance by the Social Insurance/Labor Office confirming compliance with occupational safety standards.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), Ministry of Finance; centralized e-services portal: https://www.eta.gov.eg; electronic invoice/receipt clearance platform operated by ETA for all VAT registrants.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned Egyptian LLC: (1) Appoint an ETA-recognized tax representative if no local manager is resident; (2) file registration application for the Tax Card (Bitaqa Daribiya) and VAT certificate via ETA e-services or in person at the competent tax office, attaching certified constitutional documents, POA, lease or proof of premises, board resolutions, and ID copies of shareholders/managers; (3) await ETA inspection and issuance of the unified Tax Identification Number (TIN) and VAT registration number, generally within 5–15 working days; (4) activation of e-invoicing onboarding and PIN credentials is mandatory at registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable: Egypt applies entity-level taxation and has no US-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election mechanism. Available statutory elections include: (i) consolidated corporate income tax filing for a parent holding at least 100% of one or more wholly-owned Egyptian subsidiaries; (ii) election to carry forward tax losses for up to 5 years; (iii) election to apply the Suez Canal Economic Zone (SCZONE)/Free Zone preferential exemption regime for qualifying export-oriented licensed activities; (iv) option for quarterly VAT settlement for small taxpayers below the mandatory monthly frequency; (v) election to document transfer pricing via local/master file set for advance certainty.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 500,000 annual turnover of taxable goods or services; mandatory registration applies from the first day of taxable activity once the threshold is met or exceeded. Exceptional regime: dealers in scheduled luxury goods (including certain automobiles) and non-resident suppliers of electronic services may be required to register irrespective of turnover.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory full electronic invoicing and electronic receipts integrated with the ETA central clearance platform. Invoices and receipts must be transmitted in near-real time via ETA-approved APIs using JSON/XML through an ETA Mapper or certified ERP connector, or through the ETA web portal. Each submitted invoice is validated, assigned a unique ID, UUID, and cryptographic QR/stamp, and cleared before the supply can be recorded; non-compliant invoices are rejected automatically. There is no separate physical stamping; B2C retail (including online auto parts sales) is subject to the e-receipt mandate once the registrant is onboarded by ETA wave.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (0%) for the exported automotive replacement parts and tuning accessories applies if: (i) the buyer is a non-resident and the goods are physically exported outside Egypt within 90 days of the supply date; (ii) there is a direct contractual link between the Egyptian LLC and the foreign buyer; (iii) invoices are issued in foreign currency; (iv) export proceeds are received in Egypt and surrendered through an Egyptian bank per Central Bank of Egypt instructions; (v) the taxpayer holds an approved customs export declaration. Ancillary services provided to non-resident clients (e.g., tuning configuration, after-sales remote support) also qualify for 0% if performed offshore, benefited outside Egypt, and fully documented; services consumed in Egypt are subject to 14% VAT.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (final 'Bayan' as cleared by Egyptian Customs Authority, with any EDIF/Hub electronic data)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill covering the consignment
Inward Remittance Certificate or CBE-recognized bank certificate evidencing foreign currency receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice and packing list stamped by customs control
Foreign exchange settlement acknowledgment issued by the authorised Egyptian bank (EDIF matched)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: ETA audits apply enhanced scrutiny to export zero-rating claims; failure to substantiate physical export or average FX repatriation within the CBE deadline results in full clawback of the 14% VAT plus monthly delay penalty of 2% (or fraction) capped at 100% of the assessed tax. Fraudulent claims carry a criminal fine of EGP 10,000–50,000, possible imprisonment under VAT Law No. 67/2016, and a 10-year assessment window for falsified documentation. Customs violations on export declarations may trigger separate customs penalties and bank disqualification for repeat offenders.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Egypt (CBE; Arab Republic of Egypt), operating principally under Law No. 194 of 2020 (Central Bank and Banking System Law), with exclusive authority over monetary policy, foreign exchange regulation and administration, bank licensing and supervision, payment and settlement systems, and the enforcement of capital movement and anti-money laundering rules affecting Egyptian corporate accounts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed-flexible exchange rate regime implemented through the CBE interbank system. Current account transactions (imports of automotive spare parts, supplier payments, logistics service fees, platform commissions, dividends on ordinary trade, and after-tax profit remittances to non-resident shareholders) are in principle free of prior individual CBE licensing, but must be executed through a CBE-licensed bank with correct statement purpose codes and valid underlying documentation. Capital account transactions (share capital injection, shareholder loans, equity disinvestment, loan repayments not arising from trade) remain administratively controlled by the CBE and are banked through the CBE's electronic foreign exchange registration and verification procedures for foreign direct investment. Practical convertibility hurdles include: prioritization of hard-currency allocation to essential goods during FX shortages; time drag on FX liquidity during acute external deficits; mandatory documentation of goods receipts and customs declarations (ACI/ACID) before trade-related FX conversion; and the requirement for dividend remittances to be supported by audited financial statements, a tax clearance certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), and a certificate from the company's bank confirming the legality of the underlying profits.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE foreign exchange circulars applicable to Egyptian exporters, 100% of export proceeds for goods shipped from Egypt must be repatriated to a local bank account in Egypt within 5 months from the date of the bill of lading (airway bill for e-commerce parcels), extendable for up to another 5 months only with the prior authorization of the exporter's bank and on demonstrable commercial grounds. Receipts generated through Stripe, PayPal, and other payment gateways for online sales to non-resident buyers must be swept into an Egyptian bank account in the same foreign currency or converted to EGP through the banking system within the same statutory window. The exporter must execute a declaration to the bank covering the value of shipments and the expected currency of proceeds; untimely repatriation triggers bank-level blocking of future export finance, escalation to the CBE, and administrative penalties under Law No. 194 of 2020. Proceeds not offset by verified import payments for the exporter's own business must be sold to the banking system when the CBE imposes surrender ratios; as of the current regime, the statutory framework requires full repatriation but permits hold-back in foreign currency accounts subject to CBE instructions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (EGP) / Trade Settlement Account (USD and EUR)
Operational Account (EGP) / FX Account (USD/EUR) / E-Commerce Collection Account
Capital Market / Escrow Account (USD) and Cross-Border Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: LOW for the Egyptian legal entity acting as principal treasury principal. Offshore digital EMIs (Stripe Treasury, Payoneer, Airwallex, Wise Business) cannot operate as the sole clearing and settlement bank for an Egyptian-incorporated exporter because the CBE mandates that all domestic receipt, conversion, and outward payment operations for foreign exchange be conducted through licensed banks in Egypt under Law No. 194 of 2020. Such EMIs are legally viable only as auxiliary collection concentrators for inbound e-commerce receivables (Stripe/PayPal/razorpay), with automated daily or weekly sweeps by SWIFT transfer to an Egyptian bank, or as treasury vehicles for a separate offshore sales affiliate. Structural constraints: EMIs have no Egyptian banking license, cannot hold EGP settlement accounts, cannot issue Egyptian import letters of credit, and cannot authenticate ACI customs declarations; product outages and FX conversion spreads may exceed bank rails; therefore the corporate treasury must not rely solely on EMI rails for liquidity.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorized signatories of EG_LLC must appear physically before the compliance officer at the account-opening branch in Egypt for the initial corporate onboarding and signing session. The CBE's anti-money laundering framework (Law No. 80 of 2002 and its amendments) requires banks to identify senior management and verify beneficial owners (UBOs) through face-to-face due diligence at least once at onboarding; for non-resident UBOs, Egyptian banks will accept one in-person meeting held at the bank's premises, a certified copy of the passport, and an apostilled/certified corporate resolution appointing local authorized signatories. Fully remote corporate account opening is not permitted for non-resident directors except in narrow cases where the bank performs a live video-verified E-KYC, the ultimate beneficial owner holds a valid Egyptian National ID or resident permit, and all documents are attested by an Egyptian notary; in practice the bank will require the local director or the appointed natural person attorney to appear with the original commercial registry and tax card. A power of attorney for a resident signatory must be notarized by an Egyptian notary and, if issued abroad, legalized/apostilled and officially translated into Arabic.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Corporate e-commerce structure with high transaction velocity and small average ticket size inconsistent with traditional auto-parts wholesale flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements and transaction-level export reports from Stripe/PayPal covering the last 12 months; supplier contracts and pro-forma invoices; authorized distributor certificates; detailed product catalogue; e-invoicing integration certificate from the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA); refund and chargeback policy documentation; monthly billing and logistics reconciliation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner resident in a high-risk foreign jurisdiction or jurisdiction flagged by FATF for AML deficiencies
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete UBO declaration under CBE forms; passport copies; utility bills and bank reference letters from home-country financial institutions; source-of-wealth statements; registration of the Egyptian LLC by GAFI; sworn affidavit of legal funds and business history; certificate of tax residence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital injection from a shareholder's account that is inconsistent with the company's annual revenue profile or industry peer norms
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the shareholder or investor; signed board resolution approving the capital contribution; updated share ledger of EG_LLC; CBE inward transfer documentation declaring FDI; bank reference confirming legitimacy of remitting account; employment and wealth records for natural-person investors.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments to or from sanctioned countries, restricted territories, or parties appearing on UN/EU/US/UK sanctions lists among suppliers, payment processors, or logistics warehouses
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Denied-party screening report on the entire customer–supplier–logistics chain; negative screening results against OFAC, UNSC, EU, and Egypt's CBE sanctions list; B/L and country-of-origin certificates; customs entries from NAFEZA/ACI; customer-facing terms prohibiting transshipment to embargoed markets; indemnity acknowledgments for screening updates.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the stated business model (online retail) and the physical location of inventory or warehousing, or absence of a verifiable brick-and-mortar address
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid residential/commercial lease or usufruct title for Egyptian warehouse or fulfilment center; photos of premises and inventory; third-party warehouse contracts; customs entry records; GOEIC importer registration card; VAT (sales tax) certificate; director's passport and Egyptian residency visa.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inconsistent currency flows: receipts in foreign currency from overseas platforms but operating expenses paid in EGP with low foreign exchange conversion volume
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Normalized management accounts and forecast cash-flow model; intercompany transfer pricing policy and operational payments schedule; payroll records; payment-to-supplier ledger in the local bank; copy of e-invoicing records matching revenue; a treasury statement explaining conversion, hedging, and reinvestment strategy.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inward capital for EG_LLC must arrive by SWIFT MT103 or MT202 from the foreign investor's bank to the Egyptian bank, using the corporate account name and the unique company Commercial Registry number in the beneficiary line. The remittance should cite the CBE purpose code covering foreign direct investment in a limited liability company (capital subscription), reference the GAFI investment certificate issued under Law No. 72 of 2017, and be supported by the Egyptian bank's inward remittance declaration. The bank will verify the corporate registration, the UBO resolution, and the legality of the funds; funds are typically credited to a USD or EUR capital escrow account and then converted to EGP available for operations only after CBE registration confirmation is obtained. For shareholder loans, the routing file must contain an executed loan agreement, an interest schedule at arm's-length rates, CBE loan notification, and the borrower's tax identification number; the loan must be reported to the CBE and will be subject to the 5% withholding tax on interest payments at disbursement of each coupon.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments for auto-parts inventory (thermal components, filters, bearings, brake discs, electronics, tuning accessories) from suppliers in China, Germany, UAE, and Turkey will be routed over two primary rails: (1) SWIFT MT103 clean payments for low-value, low-risk repeat orders up to the CBE/bank-set trade threshold, provided the supplier is not on a restricted list and the import is matched to a valid ACI/ACID declaration in the NAFEZA single-window system; and (2) documentary letters of credit (commercial LC) issued via SWIFT MT700 for higher-value purchase orders, with the Egyptian bank acting as confirming or advising bank through a corresponding offshore bank. For both rails, the company must maintain an importer registration card issued by the General Organization for Export and Import Control (GOEIC), the supplier commercial invoice, packing list, ocean/airway bill, certificate of origin, and the ACI cargo tracking number. The local bank will apply the current CBE foreign exchange formalities, verify that the outbound payment amount matches the customs declaration, and will reject payments where the importer's name, ACID, or product HS code is inconsistent; this verification must be completed before FX conversion to hard currency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable over-the-counter (OTC) FX forward contracts (EGP against USD, EUR, and GBP) executed with a CBE-licensed Egyptian commercial bank, coverable strictly against underlying trade receivables and supplier payables, with maximum tenor aligned to the statutory 5-month export proceeds window or the trade LC maturity, where the forward is non-speculative and fully documented.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) structures on EGP are permissible only when documented through an offshore non-resident bank counterparty outside Egypt; Egyptian-resident entities may not book speculative NDFs locally, and the arrangement requires a back-to-back underlying trade exposure, CBE-reportable documentation, and board-approval memorandum setting out the hedging rationale.

Cross-currency swap contracts (USD/EGP or EUR/EGP) permitted for longer-term treasury management of intercompany debt and shareholder loans, executed with a licensed Egyptian bank or an approved international counterparty, subject to CBE maturity-mismatch notification and the company's internal derivatives policy; the swap must be designated as a cash-flow hedge under IFRS 9 with hedge documentation maintained for tax and CBE compliance.

Sight and usance letters of credit with flexible currency netting and banker's acceptances, used as an implicit hedging and financing rail by fixing the FX rate at LC issuance for the future payment date.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return (Form 47) with audited financial statements and tax reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year end; for a 31 December year-end, due by 30 April.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly delay penalty of up to 2% of the unpaid tax plus administrative fines; persistent default triggers tax attachment, legal enforcement and criminal referral.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and ordinary general assembly minutes filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) – Companies Registration Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year end; the ordinary general assembly must approve the accounts before the same deadline.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative warning and fines under Companies Law No. 159/1981; repeated non-compliance may result in suspension of company registration and strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal declaration (Shahr Al-Tijari)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI one-stop-shop / Commercial Registry under the Ministry of Justice
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by 31 January for the calendar year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee per month of delay, administrative fine, and eventual suspension or strike-off from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial ownership and register confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: GAFI – Beneficial Ownership Register (under AML Law No. 80/2002)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation within 30 days after the ordinary general assembly; event-driven update within 15 days of any shareholding or control change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EGP 1,000,000 under AML Law No. 80/2002; registration file may be suspended.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No revenue or asset threshold; every Egyptian LLC must appoint a certified auditor and file audited financial statements under Companies Law No. 159/1981 and Income Tax Law No. 91/2005.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are aligned with IFRS; fully IFRS-compliant accounts are acceptable where required by parent or regulator.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annually, the LLC must review and confirm its beneficial ownership schedules with GAFI within 30 days of the general assembly approving the annual financial statements. Any transfer of shares or change in control requires an update within 15 days. The register must show legal name, nationality, ownership percentage, control nature and source of funds.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minutes of Shareholders' Meeting and Resolutions

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Standard rate applies to an online retail LLC; no automatic tax holiday. An elective incentive under Investment Law No. 72/2017 allows newly established companies in less-developed governorates to deduct up to 50% of qualifying fixed asset investment from taxable income; projects licensed in the Suez Canal Economic Zone or investment zones may obtain preferential treatment (e.g., 20% rate or 1% free-zone annual fee) if they obtain a formal investment certificate. Loss-carryforward and export-related deductions are available under Law No. 91 of 2005.
